function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in the context of financial services—especially mutual funds, ETFs, or other investment products—is a formal authorization that allows a fund manager or a financial institution to act on behalf of an investor. It’s essentially a legal agreement that gives the manager the right to buy, sell, or manage assets within a specified account. Key points about a mandate: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Enables the manager to execute trades, rebalance portfolios, or perform other investment actions without needing the investor’s explicit approval for each transaction. | | **Types** | • **Active Mandate** – Manager has full discretion to trade.
• **Passive/Discretionary Mandate** – Manager follows a pre‑agreed strategy but still has some flexibility.
• **Non‑discretionary Mandate** – Investor retains control; manager only executes orders upon receiving instructions. | | **Duration** | Usually set for a specific period (e.g., one year) and can be renewed or terminated by either party. | | **Legal Binding** | It’s a contract, so both parties have rights and obligations. | | **Common Use Cases** | • Portfolio management for high‑net‑worth individuals.
• Institutional investors delegating day‑to‑day trading to asset managers.
• Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) where the mandate authorizes regular contributions and rebalancing. | In short, a mandate is the formal permission that lets a manager handle your investments according to agreed terms, providing convenience and professional oversight while ensuring legal clarity.
